claims.text: A predictive methodology incorporating atomic-scale lattice-distortion and mass-disorder metrics can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with lower phonon thermal conductivity than conventional bulk-averaged models predict.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr can represent a homogeneous, single-phase high-entropy alloy with a stable BCC or related structure and minimal secondary-phase formation.
Controlled processing routes can minimize extrinsic defects in the synthesized candidate alloys.
Minimizing grain-boundary and processing-induced effects allows intrinsic phonon transport to be isolated.
Enhanced local lattice distortions and mass-disorder scattering centers limit the phonon mean free path.
Increased chemical complexity and atomic-size mismatch create heterogeneous local atomic environments in the selected high-entropy alloys.
Heterogeneous local atomic environments act as efficient phonon-scattering centers.
The proposed phonon-scattering mechanism significantly reduces phonon thermal conductivity.
Candidates identified by the proposed method will have at least 20% lower phonon thermal conductivity than comparable alloys selected or predicted using traditional average-property models.
Traditional baseline models use average lattice parameters and elastic properties without accounting for local disorder.
The predictive capability applies to well-homogenized, near-equiatomic, single-phase high-entropy alloys.
The predictive capability may fail when significant secondary phases are present.
The predictive capability may fail at high oxygen or contaminant levels.
The predictive capability may fail when processing-induced defects dominate thermal transport.
The expected improvement corresponds to approximately 20–30% lower phonon thermal conductivity.
Local lattice-distortion metrics should correlate meaningfully with measured phonon thermal conductivity across the tested alloy series.
